title: SkinCancerCapstone: Transfer-learning classifier for malignant vs. benign dermoscopic skin lesions (v5, leak-free evaluation)
description:
Code and model for a binary classifier (malignant vs. benign) of dermoscopic skin-lesion images, using a frozen ImageNet ResNet50 and a small trained classification head.

Data. Kaggle "Skin Cancer: Malignant vs. Benign" (ISIC-derived): 2,637 training and 660 test images at 224x224. A perceptual-hash search with visual confirmation found 24 test images that duplicate a training lesion; they were excluded, leaving 636 test images.

Method. Learning rate, dropout and number of epochs were chosen by 5-fold stratified group cross-validation on training data only (near-duplicate lesions kept within one fold). The chosen model (learning rate 0.001, dropout 0.2, 26 epochs) was retrained on all training data and scored on the test set once.

Results. Test accuracy 89.8% (95% CI 87.4-92.0%), sensitivity 92.6%, specificity 87.6%, PPV 85.6%, ROC AUC 0.957. Cross-validated accuracy 89.0 +/- 1.5%.

Educational research project; not a medical device or diagnostic tool.
